subject: English
description: A/an/the rules: indefinite vs definite, zero article, with abstract/proper nouns

questions.stem: Choose the correct articles: '___ honest man is ___ asset to ___ society.'

options.option_text: A / a / a (all indefinite forms here)
The / the / the (all definite forms used)
An / a / the (mixed articles all together)

questions.explanation: 'Honest' starts with silent H (vowel sound) → 'AN honest'. 'Asset' starts with vowel → 'AN asset'. 'Society' is an abstract/general noun used in a general sense → ZERO article (Ø). Rule of articles before H: silent H takes 'an' (an hour, an honour, an honest); pronounced H takes 'a' (a hospital, a hotel, a house).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Pick the correct article: 'He is ___ MBA from ___ IIM Bangalore.'
questions.explanation: MBA pronounced 'em-bee-ay' starts with VOWEL SOUND ('em') → AN MBA. Names of specific institutions like IIM Bangalore (when used with location) take ZERO article. (Compare: 'he is at the IIM' — generic — vs. 'he studied at IIM Bangalore' — proper noun + place). Rule for letters/abbreviations: F, H, L, M, N, R, S, X start with vowel sound → 'an' (an FIR, an MA, an X-ray).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: '___ Ganges is ___ holiest river in India.'
questions.explanation: Rule 1: rivers, oceans, seas, mountain ranges take THE (the Ganges, the Nile, the Arabian Sea, the Himalayas). Rule 2: superlatives (holiest, biggest, smallest) always take THE. So 'THE Ganges' + 'THE holiest river'. Mountains as a single peak don't take 'the' (Mount Everest, Mount Fuji).

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: 'She plays ___ piano but doesn't play ___ cricket.'

options.option_text: The / Ø (definite for instrument, none for sport)
The / the (definite for both terms used)

questions.explanation: Rule: musical INSTRUMENTS take THE (play THE piano, the guitar, the violin). SPORTS take ZERO article (play cricket, play football, play chess). Common SSC/banking error → using 'the' before sports. Memorize the pair: instruments WITH 'the', sports WITHOUT.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Fill in: '___ Mahatma Gandhi led ___ Indian freedom movement.'
questions.explanation: Rule: titles + proper nouns of fame take THE (the Mahatma, the Father of the Nation, the Iron Lady). Specific historical movements/events take THE (the Indian freedom movement, the French Revolution, the Cold War). 'Gandhi' alone takes Ø; 'THE Mahatma Gandhi' uses the title-form.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose: 'I had ___ uniform on, while waiting for ___ university bus.'
questions.explanation: 'Uniform', 'university', 'European', 'one-way' begin with the CONSONANT SOUND /yu:/ → take A (not 'an'), even though spelled with vowel U/E/O. Rule: articles depend on the SOUND not the LETTER. 'A uniform' (yu-niform) but 'An umbrella' (uh-mbrella).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Pick the correct article: '___ rich should help ___ poor.'

options.option_text: Ø / Ø (no article needed at all)

questions.explanation: Rule: ADJECTIVES used as PLURAL NOUNS to refer to a class take THE. 'The rich' = rich people; 'the poor' = poor people; 'the elderly', 'the deaf', 'the blind', 'the unemployed'. Acts as a generic plural — verb agrees in plural form (the rich ARE generous).
